correctness.rationale: Since every immunity factor lies in \([0,1]\), the effective reproduction number is at most \(\tau\); therefore \(\tau<1\) forces zero outbreak. Repeating the exact no-outbreak update \(r-1\) times sends every population vector to \((0,\ldots,0,1)\) and makes each retained immunity coordinate a product of only within-block drift factors. Conditional on all \(r-1\) transmissibilities being below one, the terminal law is thus independent of the incoming state. The event has probability \(\beta^{r-1}\), giving the claimed Doeblin decomposition and contraction. The edge case \(\beta=1\) is also valid because the \((r-1)\)-step kernel is then state-independent. The exact verifier independently confirms the finite-memory coalescence for \(2\le r\le12\); the universal proof is algebraic.

final_claim: For the Britton–Pugliese multi-season epidemic chain with \(r\ge2\), iid seasonal pairs and \(\beta=\mathbb P(\tau<1)>0\), an \((r-1)\)-season no-outbreak block gives a state-independent minorization of mass \(\beta^{r-1}\), hence a unique stationary law and the stated uniform geometric total-variation contraction without any complete-drift atom or density assumption.
limitations: Seasonal pairs remain iid across seasons; within-season drift/transmissibility dependence is allowed.
The rate is a guaranteed block rate, not an optimal mixing constant.
